issues.description: The Vietnamese line can sound ambiguous because ốm can mean thin in some contexts, and it feels a little stronger than You look sick. A clearer and more natural line would say Ben looks unwell.
issues.suggested_fix: Ben ơi, trông bạn có vẻ không khỏe.

issues.description: The target-word gloss for headache is understandable, but when your head feels sick is not the clearest meaning for A2 learners. The Vietnamese gloss could also be the direct, common phrase.
issues.suggested_fix: headache gloss: en = when your head hurts; vi = đau đầu

issues.description: For sick, bị ốm is acceptable, but it can feel dialect-dependent or ambiguous. A slightly clearer Vietnamese gloss would include bị bệnh or không khỏe.
issues.suggested_fix: sick gloss vi: bị bệnh, cảm thấy không khỏe

issues.description: The hook is clear but a little flat. A question hook would make me more curious to listen on my commute.
issues.suggested_fix: Hook: Ben has a headache. Should he go to work?

qa_report.summary: This micro-dialogue is short, clear, and suitable for A2 learners. The grammar point is easy to notice, and the target and review words appear naturally. I could follow it easily. The main edits are small Vietnamese naturalness improvements and a clearer gloss for headache. After those edits, I would happily listen and learn.
